question: Where is the COLDEST capital city on Earth?

post.premise: The only capital city that averages below freezing
post.bait: It is not in Canada, and it is not Moscow.
keywords: coldest capital city in the world
post.sources_line: WorldAtlas; Wikipedia (Ulaanbaatar, NOAA 1991–2020 normals); National Statistics Office of Mongolia; Britannica

youtube.title: Which country has the coldest capital city on Earth? Not Canada 🥶
youtube.description:
Canada, Kazakhstan or the third one? One capital city averages below freezing across the whole year, and it is the only one that does.
Guess before the map fills in, then see the altitude that explains it and how much of the country lives there.
One map fact a day you can argue about — follow along.

threads.text: Where is the coldest capital city on Earth — Canada, Kazakhstan or Mongolia? Only one national capital averages below freezing across a whole year, it sits higher than most ski resorts, and about half the country's people live in it.

intent: The capital nobody files under cold: three cold-country flags, one answer with a sub-zero yearly average, the altitude that explains it, and the fact that half a nation lives in it.

v04.text: Mongolia. Ulaanbaatar is the only capital on Earth whose average temperature, over the whole year, is below freezing.

v05.text: January nights there pass minus 30. Astana, in Kazakhstan, is second; Ottawa is not close.

v06.text: The secret is height: the city sits over 1,300 metres up, on a plateau far from any ocean.

v07.text: And about half of all Mongolians live in it, more than 1,600,000 people in a single cold valley.

v08.text: Colder than you thought. Follow us.

research.topic: Coldest national capital: Ulaanbaatar, Mongolia — the only capital with a sub-zero annual mean (≈ −0.4 to −1.3 °C depending on period); Astana second; altitude ~1,350 m; January nights below −30 °C; ~1.6 million people, about half of Mongolia's ~3.5 million

myths.myth: Ottawa or Moscow is the coldest capital.
myths.reality: Ulaanbaatar is the only national capital whose annual mean temperature is below 0 °C; Astana is second; Ottawa and Moscow both average several degrees above freezing.
